sections.prose: At the public entry, `new_memory_face` passes the original `data` bytes, `face_index`, and `size_pt` to `memory_face`; a `FontError` propagates through `?`. On success, the bytes have become a `Face` holding the parsed font and a default `render_fonts` cache—the glyph bitmap is a later step. In `memory_face`, the first probes route a PCF version to its driver, then the `PFR0` prefix to `pfr_face`, then two WinFNT versions; a BDF-like first keyword is checked by `parse_bdf_constructor_error` before `bdf_face` is called. That BDF guard is an exception to the simple format-to-constructor rule: it can return its parse error without constructing a face.

sections.title: SFNT parsing feeds a flag-driven glyph request
sections.prose: After the earlier prefix probes, `memory_face` checks `type42_sfnt_data` and `type1_cleartext`, rejects an all-control stream of at least 17 bytes, then tries `truetype_face`. If that fails and the buffer is at least 118 bytes, `winfnt_face` gets a retry: success wins, a shaped WinFNT header can preserve `UnknownFileFormat`, but other failures leave the original TrueType error intact. For SFNT, `truetype_face_with_load_mode_and_design_coords` uses the low 16 bits of `face_index` to `resolve_face_index` and `parse_table_directory_at`, then reads tables. Missing `head`, `maxp`, `cmap`, `hhea`, or `hmtx` aborts opening, and `parse_head` errors propagate; malformed `maxp`, `cmap`, and `hmtx` instead default through `parse_maxp`, `parse_cmap`, and `parse_hmtx`. The glyph request begins at `load_glyph`, which forwards its index and flags; `load_glyph_from_font` calls `normalize_load_flags` before choosing a route. Zero ppem or `NO_RECURSE` forces `NO_SCALE`, which forces `NO_HINTING | NO_BITMAP` and clears `RENDER`; `BITMAP_METRICS_ONLY` also clears `RENDER`. Before scalable outlines, `sbix_active_strike_is_unmatched` returns `InvalidPixelSize`, while `sbix_missing_bitmap_glyph` instead returns a successful empty slot. When `COLOR` is set and `NO_SVG` is clear, `load_svg_glyph` returns an SVG slot on success; an unavailable glyph errors only for `svg_only`, otherwise loading continues, and `svg_only` also errors if SVG was not allowed. An embedded strike is `sbit_allowed` unless `NO_SCALE` is set or both `NO_BITMAP` and a scalable face apply, so `NO_BITMAP` alone does not suppress strikes for a bitmap-only face. A forbidden or missing strike becomes an error only with `sbits_only`; otherwise failure falls through to outline loading, while success may `flatten_bgra_to_gray` and returns the strike slot.

sections.title: The TrueType branch loads, scales, and hints outlines
sections.prose: Inside `load_glyph_from_font`, `LoadFlags` form an ordered choice: `NO_RECURSE`, `NO_SCALE`, then `NO_HINTING` take precedence; `FORCE_AUTOHINT` applies only without `NO_AUTOHINT`, then target-light, explicit no-autohint, and finally the default loader. Errors from whichever selected loader uses `?` propagate instead of falling through to the next hint mode. The regular `glyph_slot_load_default_with_layout_and_mode_and_hdmx_and_pedantic` route diverts Type 1 faces to their driver and empty CID Type 1 faces to an empty outline. Other faces use `scale_glyph_for_metrics_default_with_mode_and_hdmx_and_pedantic`: both `fpgm` and `cvt` select a prepared native-bytecode context; without that pair, `should_use_default_autohint` selects the default auto-hinter, otherwise the outline is simply scaled, with `native_hint_mode` passed to the matching auto-hint branch. Pathological native metrics can also fall back to auto-hinting while preserving advance. `load_glyph_outline` uses the CFF driver without caching its stateful CFF outlines, but caches CFF2 and TrueType results in `glyph_cache`. For TrueType, an active variation with `gvar` takes `load_glyph_with_variations`; otherwise `load_glyph` decodes the ordinary `glyf` outline, which is then cached. TrueType `load_glyph` enters `load_glyph_inner`; `get_glyph_location` reads short, doubled or long `loca` offsets, and some out-of-table or zero-length ranges become an empty `GlyphLocation`. A missing public glyph index is `InvalidArgument`, a missing component is `InvalidComposite`, and recursion deeper than 100 or a short `glyf` record fails; nonnegative contour counts parse a simple `GlyphOutline`, while composites recursively load components. For native TrueType hinting, `hint_glyph` builds a `GlyphZone` from scaled and original points plus four phantom metric points, then clones `prepared_context` and executes the glyph instruction stream with `run_program`. An instruction error is returned only in pedantic mode; otherwise the partially interpreted zone continues into coordinate write-back, so native hints are not a blanket requirement for success.
